monday.definition: The day after Sunday and before Tuesday.
monday.exampleUsage: Maya has a meeting on Monday.

tuesday.definition: The day after Monday and before Wednesday.

wednesday.definition: The day after Tuesday and before Thursday.

thursday.definition: The day after Wednesday and before Friday.
thursday.exampleUsage: The team reviews the plan on Thursday.

friday.definition: The day after Thursday and before Saturday.

saturday.definition: The day after Friday and before Sunday.
saturday.exampleUsage: Maya visits a friend on Saturday.

sunday.definition: The day after Saturday and before Monday.

weekday.definition: A day that is not part of the weekend in a particular place.
weekday.arabicTranslation: يوم من أيام الأسبوع غير عطلة نهاية الأسبوع
weekday.exampleUsage: Maya works each weekday from Monday to Friday.

weekend.definition: The days at the end of a working week when many people do not work.
weekend.exampleUsage: Saturday and Sunday are Maya’s weekend.

day-off.definition: A day when a person does not have to go to work or school.
day-off.exampleUsage: Maya has a day off on Sunday.

january.definition: The first month of the year in the Gregorian calendar.
january.exampleUsage: Maya plans the course in January.

february.definition: The month following January and preceding March in the Gregorian calendar.

march.definition: The month following February and preceding April in the Gregorian calendar.

april.definition: The month following March and preceding May in the Gregorian calendar.
april.exampleUsage: The next class is in April.

may.definition: The month following April and preceding June in the Gregorian calendar.

june.definition: The month following May and preceding July in the Gregorian calendar.
june.exampleUsage: This college year ends in June.

july.definition: The month following June and preceding August in the Gregorian calendar.
july.exampleUsage: Maya takes a short course in July.

august.definition: The month following July and preceding September in the Gregorian calendar.

september.definition: The month following August and preceding October in the Gregorian calendar.
september.exampleUsage: This college year starts in September.

october.definition: The month following September and preceding November in the Gregorian calendar.
october.exampleUsage: The next report is in October.

november.definition: The month following October and preceding December in the Gregorian calendar.
november.exampleUsage: The team reviews the plan in November.

december.definition: The last (12th) month of the year in the Gregorian calendar.

leap-year.definition: A Gregorian calendar year with 366 days, including February 29.
leap-year.exampleUsage: A Gregorian leap year has an extra day in February.

fiscal-year.definition: A twelve-month period used to plan and report an organization's finances.
fiscal-year.exampleUsage: The office uses a fiscal year for its accounts.

academic-year.definition: The part of the year when a school or university holds classes.
academic-year.exampleUsage: This college’s academic year starts in September.

calendar-year.definition: In the Gregorian calendar, the period from January 1 to December 31.
calendar-year.exampleUsage: The Gregorian calendar year begins in January.

quarter.definition: One of four three-month periods in a year.
quarter.exampleUsage: The office divides the year into four quarters.

semester.definition: One of two divisions of an academic year.
semester.exampleUsage: The first semester ends in December.

trimester.definition: One of three divisions of an academic year.
trimester.exampleUsage: This institution divides its academic year into three trimesters.

biannual.definition: Happening twice a year in this context.
biannual.exampleUsage: The biannual report appears twice a year.

today.definition: The day that is happening now.

tomorrow.definition: The day immediately after the present day.
tomorrow.exampleUsage: The next task is due tomorrow.

this-week.definition: The seven-day period that includes the present day, according to the calendar system being used.
this-week.exampleUsage: We have two meetings this week.

next-week.definition: The week immediately after the current week.

last-week.definition: The week immediately before the current week.
last-week.exampleUsage: We visited the museum last week.

this-month.definition: The calendar month that includes the present day.
this-month.exampleUsage: The club meets twice this month.

next-month.definition: The calendar month immediately after the current month.
next-month.exampleUsage: The new course begins next month.

last-month.definition: The calendar month immediately before the current month.
last-month.exampleUsage: The team finished the task last month.

this-year.definition: The calendar year that includes the present date.
this-year.exampleUsage: We are studying a new subject this year.

date.definition: A particular day shown by its day, month, and year.

appointment.definition: A planned meeting with a person at a particular time.
appointment.exampleUsage: Hana has an appointment at nine.

schedule.definition: A plan that shows when activities or events will happen.
schedule.exampleUsage: The work schedule shows a meeting at nine.

planner.definition: A notebook or calendar used to organize tasks, dates, and appointments.
planner.exampleUsage: Hana opens her planner before work.

diary.definition: A book for recording appointments or daily events; here an appointment diary.
diary.exampleUsage: Hana writes the appointment in her diary.

agenda.definition: A list of planned activities or topics; here the day’s work plan.
agenda.exampleUsage: Today’s agenda includes a meeting and a call.

deadline.definition: The latest time by which something must be finished.

reminder.definition: A message that helps you remember something.
reminder.exampleUsage: A reminder helps Hana remember the event.

event.definition: Something planned to happen at a particular time, such as a celebration or meeting.

calendar.definition: A system or display that organises days, weeks and months.
calendar.exampleUsage: Hana checks the date on her calendar.
